# Debrief: Argo CD

These clips show Argo CD teams how others adopted GitOps and Rollouts, previewed pull request changes, added MCP automation, paired it with Crossplane and OPA, and avoided gateway migration pitfalls. ([From FTP To Argo CD & Argo Rollouts: An Adoption History Inside a Corp · 0:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wrek7kjrcs0&t=0s); [Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 5:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=326s); [The 10x DevOps Engineer’s Toolkit: Argo CD + AI-Driven MCP Automation · 7:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iC15zeOLZQA&t=472s); [Backend-First IDP: A Production Roadmap With Argo CD, Crossplane, and OPA · 18:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q2b9niAdFII&t=1134s); [From ingress-nginx to Envoy Gateway at Zapier: The Benefits, Challenges, and Migration Lessons That Matter · 8:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIj2U13VZJY&t=531s))

## Top 3 takeaways

1. Argo CD's GitOps model is declarative and self-correcting: you define the desired state, and the system watches for drift and pulls it back to match the repo definition. ([From FTP To Argo CD & Argo Rollouts: An Adoption History Inside a Corp · 12:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wrek7kjrcs0&t=737s))
2. A real Argo CD instance can render manifests for pull request previews, matching production configuration. Speed was the main downside, and it has been the focus of recent improvements. ([Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 5:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=326s))
3. Argo CD features such as self-healing, ApplicationSets across clusters, sync waves and pre-sync hooks can be combined with Argo Workflows, Events and Rollouts in one automated loop. ([GitOps Your Costs: Automated FinOps Through Argo Workflows · 14:23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x5nVyVZSd0A&t=863s); [GitOps Your Costs: Automated FinOps Through Argo Workflows · 16:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x5nVyVZSd0A&t=1002s))

## Action items

- [ ] Try an Argo Rollouts canary with QA-authored analysis stages that must pass before the rollout advances, as shown in the adoption demo. ([From FTP To Argo CD & Argo Rollouts: An Adoption History Inside a Corp · 18:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wrek7kjrcs0&t=1137s))
- [ ] Evaluate the MCP server for Argo CD, whose tools map one-to-one to CLI and UI actions such as sync, logs and live manifests, and give feedback to the project. ([The 10x DevOps Engineer’s Toolkit: Argo CD + AI-Driven MCP Automation · 7:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iC15zeOLZQA&t=472s))
- [ ] If you plan to move ingress to Envoy Gateway, check how encoded paths are handled, since Argo CD paths returned 404 until escaped slashes were kept unchanged. ([From ingress-nginx to Envoy Gateway at Zapier: The Benefits, Challenges, and Migration Lessons That Matter · 8:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIj2U13VZJY&t=531s))

## Watch together (11 min)

1. [From FTP To Argo CD & Argo Rollouts: An Adoption History Inside a Corp · 12:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wrek7kjrcs0&t=737s) (1:19), Alfonso Ming, Meritxell Rodríguez: Clear explanation of declarative GitOps, drift correction and Argo CD as source of truth.
2. [Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 5:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=326s) (3:32), Dag Bjerre Andersen, Sergey Shevchenko: Practical approach to previewing pull request changes using real Argo CD rendering.
3. [The 10x DevOps Engineer’s Toolkit: Argo CD + AI-Driven MCP Automation · 7:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iC15zeOLZQA&t=472s) (2:21), Alexander Matyushentsev, Leonardo Luz Almeida: Shows what the Argo CD MCP server can do and its production use.
4. [From ingress-nginx to Envoy Gateway at Zapier: The Benefits, Challenges, and Migration Lessons That Matter · 8:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIj2U13VZJY&t=531s) (2:27), Kalen Wessel: Warns of an Argo CD 404 caused by path normalization.
5. [Backend-First IDP: A Production Roadmap With Argo CD, Crossplane, and OPA · 18:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q2b9niAdFII&t=1134s) (1:20), Abhinav Sharma, Aditya Soni: Demo of Git commits driving changes through Argo CD and Crossplane without a UI.
